title: Looking for advice about art pipeline
author: korvelar
selftext:
Hello! Game developer here.

I'm exploring ways how to build effective AI art generation pipeline and I'm bogged down in a multitude of tools and services.

How I see the workflow: concept art from text descriptions → extracting game assets: characters, props, items, UI maintained in the same style → editing, variations for each image → animations.

I'm looking mostly for pixel art. 

I want to have all my assets in common context to keep consistency in style.

What tool or set of tools can you advise?

comments.author: liuyj3000
comments.body:
I've been working on a similar pipeline for pixel art game assets. Here's what's worked well for me:

**Concept Art / Base Generation**

- **ComfyUI + Stable Diffusion** (SDXL or SD 1.5 with pixel art LoRAs) — this is the backbone. ComfyUI's node-based workflow lets you build repeatable pipelines. There are great pixel art checkpoints on Civitai (look for ones trained specifically on 16x16 or 32x32 if that's your target resolution).
- For text-to-image consistency, build a base prompt template with your style keywords and reuse it across all generations.

**Style Consistency**

- Use **IP-Adapter** in ComfyUI — feed it a reference image of your established style and it'll keep new generations consistent without fine-tuning.
- If you need tighter control, train a **LoRA on your own approved assets** (even 10-20 images works). This becomes your "style lock."

**Asset Extraction & Editing**

- **Remove backgrounds** with rembg or BiRefNet node in ComfyUI (works great for sprites).
- For variations (different poses, color swaps), use **img2img with ControlNet** — specifically the lineart or canny preprocessor to keep shapes consistent while varying details.

**Animation**

- This is still the weakest link in AI pipelines honestly. Best current options:
- **Aseprite** for manual pixel art animation (still the gold standard)
- **PixelOver** if you want to interpolate between keyframes
- For AI-assisted: generate keyframes with SD, then use Aseprite to clean up and tween

**Workflow tip:** Keep a "style bible" folder — 5-10 approved reference images that define your look. Feed these into IP-Adapter or use them as img2img inputs for every new asset. This is the single most important thing for consistency across a whole project.

What's your target resolution and game genre? Happy to give more specific recommendations.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
AI is super helpful but I think people who aren’t “in it” overestimate how much ai actually accomplishes for the user. OP hasn’t said anything about getting his ideas from AI. 

Personally, I started with having ai generate sprites for me but I have had to edit so much to fit the style of my game that now I’m basically just using gen ai for reference.

Not going to lie, I’m heavily relying on ai for code but I’m always explaining what I want to be done, most of the time it’s a long planning phase where I’m learning and making sure codex isn’t going to do something stupid with my scripts. Values are almost always tweaked.

comments.author: inakura1234321
comments.body: I've been doing "neurosymbolic" generation which has worked pretty well for me. Essentially vibe coding a library of 3d csg generators and baking into pixel art sprites using a lot of postprocessing or exporting for 3d

comments.author: SeekingSpire
comments.body:
If you're willing to put time into learning something and have the hardware to host a diffusion model locally:  
  
"[Pixaroma](https://www.youtube.com/@pixaroma)" is probably the greatest teacher / source of free information on ComfyUI that I've found. Learning Comfy and adapting workflows is a powerful move. A nice side note is that that Claude Code/Codex can understand and modify the JSON workflows and help you understand accurate prompting techniques for each checkpoint type (SDXL, Flux, WAN, etc.).

Another fantastic creator is "[Mickmumpitz](https://www.youtube.com/@mickmumpitz)" who offers both free and Patreon tier workflows for consistent character generation and similar workflows. Again focused on ComfyUI (self hosted)..
